svg.title: The Event Loop in Detail
svg.desc: Auto-playing 72s step-by-step explainer of "The Event Loop in Detail" (from img_8.png). Each step is highlighted in turn with what happens, why it matters, missing concepts added in lime, and a Node.js code example. Hover to pause.
svg.text: The phases of one loop tick, the callback queue in each phase, and the microtask queues that run in between
↻ any pending timers or I/O? YES → next loop tick · NO → exit program
Most of your code runs here

g.text: What: Each loop tick goes through phases in a fixed order, and each phase has its own
callback queue: expired timers → I/O polling → setImmediate → close callbacks.
Why: This order decides which callback runs first: a favourite interview puzzle.
Added: The real libuv order has a "pending callbacks" phase the slide skips, and microtasks
run after EVERY callback (Node 11+), not only between phases.
What: First, callbacks of timers whose time is up (setTimeout, setInterval). A 100 ms timer
is a minimum delay, not an exact one.
Why: Timers vs setImmediate order is NOT guaranteed in the main module, but inside an I/O
// from main module: order NOT guaranteed
What: Some I/O callbacks are deferred to the next tick, e.g. some TCP errors. libuv also has
Why: The slide simplifies this away; you rarely touch it, but it completes the real phase
What: Polls for new I/O events and runs their callbacks: finished file reads, incoming data
on sockets. 99% of app code runs here.
Why: When nothing else is due, the loop blocks here waiting for I/O, using zero CPU.
// no timers due + no setImmediate queued
// → the loop waits here for I/O (no CPU used)
What: setImmediate callbacks run right after the poll phase of the current tick.
Why: Use it to run something right after the current I/O batch, without waiting for the
// it runs in the check phase, after I/O polling
What: Close events, like a socket or server closing, run last in the tick.
What: Two special queues run as soon as the current callback ends: first all
process.nextTick callbacks, then all resolved-promise callbacks.
Added: Since Node 11 they run after every single callback, not only between phases. A
recursive nextTick never lets the loop move on.
What: After the close phase Node checks for pending timers or I/O. Yes → another tick. No →
Added: unref() tells Node not to stay alive just for that timer or socket.
t.unref(); // don't keep the process alive for this
What: timers → pending → poll (I/O) → check (setImmediate) → close → repeat or exit.
nextTick and promise microtasks squeeze in after every callback.

svg.text: Phases: timers, pending, poll, check, close
Thinking nextTick runs on the "next tick"
→ it runs before the loop moves on at all
Q: setTimeout(0) vs setImmediate vs nextTick?
A: nextTick first; inside I/O immediate first
